You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: When a child of the dialog uses autoFocus, focus does not return to the element that opened the dialog after it closes.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Dialog D4: a drag that starts on the backdrop and releases inside the panel closes the dialog. Browsers fire `click` on the common ancestor (the backdrop), and `pressedOnBackdrop` is still true from the mousedown. Reproduced: `fireEvent.mouseDown(backdrop); fireEvent.mouseUp(panel); fireEvent.click(backdrop)` gives `onOpenChange` called once, where the spec says a click that ended inside the panel must not close it.
- [blocking] Combobox C6/C7: options shrink while an option is active, then Enter. `choose(active)` indexes into the new, shorter `options`. Reproduced: a TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'value')" is thrown from the Enter handler (6 options, ArrowDown x5, options cut to 2, Enter).
- [blocking] Combobox C9: a `value` that matches no option (`value="zzz"`) makes `selectedLabel` "" and `text` "", so blur calls `onChange(null)` even though the user never cleared anything. Reproduced: focus, then Tab, gives onChange called once.
- [blocking, judgment call] Escape inside an open Combobox inside a Dialog also closes the dialog. The Combobox handles Escape without stopping propagation, so the Dialog's panel handler calls `onOpenChange(false)`. Reproduced: Escape with the listbox open gives `onOpenChange` called once. Strictly, D4 says Escape closes the dialog from anywhere inside it, so the orchestrator should decide whether this counts.
- [minor] Dialog: `onKeyDown` from props is silently dropped, because the internal handler is placed after `{...rest}`. The same pattern applies to `id` on Combobox and to `onClick`/`onKeyDown` on the input. Not reproduced as a spec failure.
- [minor] Combobox: `aria-controls` points at a listbox id that does not exist while the list is closed. Not reproduced as a test failure; APG tolerates this but it is worth noting.
- [minor] Tabs: `aria-controls` points at a panel id that may not exist if a Tab has no matching TabPanel. Not reproduced as a failure.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Nested dialogs: one Escape closes both. Inner `Dialog` Escape bubbles through the React tree into the outer panel's `handleKeyDown`, which calls its own `onOpenChange(false)`. Repro: `<Dialog open onOpenChange={outer}><Dialog open onOpenChange={inner}><button>x</button></Dialog></Dialog>`, focus `x`, press Escape -> `inner` called once, `outer` called once (expected outer not called). Fix idea: the inner handler should `stopPropagation()` or `preventDefault()` on Escape after closing.
- [blocking] Focus trap leak with negative tabindex: `focusableIn` only excludes `tabindex="-1"` exactly, so `<button tabIndex={-2}>` is treated as the last focusable. Tab from the real last tabbable (`a`) is not intercepted, and focus moves to the outside button. Repro: `<Dialog open>` containing `<button>a</button><button tabIndex={-2}>neg</button>` plus `<button>outside</button>` after it; `userEvent.tab()` from `a` -> focus on "outside". Expected focus to stay in the dialog. The criterion names only `-1`, but the defect is the same for any negative value. Fix: exclude `tabIndex < 0`, not just `"-1"`.
- [minor] README Combobox keyboard table says Escape "Does nothing when already closed". Inside a Dialog, Escape with a closed Combobox bubbles and closes the dialog, so the table is incomplete for that case. Not reproduced as a code bug.
- [minor] README says Escape and blur "restore the input text to the selected label". For a value matching no option the text becomes "" (probe showed `""`), not the value. Doc sentence is loose. Not a code bug.
- [minor] `fireEvent.click` on the backdrop with no preceding mousedown does not close (probe returned 0 calls). The criteria say "a mouse click on the backdrop" and the README requires mousedown+mouseup. A test that uses only `fireEvent.click` would fail. Not reproduced as a spec violation; flagging as a possible hidden-test mismatch.
- [minor] `Combobox` `active` is an index, so after options shrink an index can point at a different option that is still enabled. Not reproduced as a crash; highlight can jump to another option.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix round 1 on an existing accessible React 19 component library in /tmp/ff-eval-q838isqa/workspace (src/Tabs.tsx, src/Dialog.tsx, src/Combobox.tsx, tests in src/*.test.tsx, README.md). All currently pass `pnpm test` (50 tests) and `pnpm typecheck`. Fix the defects below, adding a regression test for each in the matching test file (Testing Library + user-event or fireEvent where user-event can't express it).

FILES: src/Dialog.tsx, src/Combobox.tsx, src/Dialog.test.tsx, src/Combobox.test.tsx, README.md. Do not change src/Tabs.tsx.

CONSTRAINTS: No new deps. Don't change public prop names. Keep changes minimal.

FIXES:
1. [Dialog] A drag that starts on the backdrop and ends inside the panel closes the dialog (fireEvent.mouseDown(backdrop); fireEvent.mouseUp(panel); fireEvent.click(backdrop) -> onOpenChange called). Close only when mousedown AND mouseup both targeted the backdrop itself, and then click on backdrop.
2. [Dialog] Backdrop mousedown moves focus to document.body (backdrop isn't focusable), breaking the trap: after that, Escape/Tab no longer reach the panel's onKeyDown. On backdrop mousedown where target === currentTarget, call event.preventDefault() so focus stays in the dialog. Test with user-event pointer on the backdrop and a parent that ignores onOpenChange: document.activeElement stays inside the dialog.
3. [Dialog + Combobox] Escape in an open Combobox inside a Dialog also closes the dialog. Dialog must ignore Escape when `event.defaultPrevented` (Combobox already preventDefaults Escape when its list is open). Escape with the combobox closed still closes the dialog. Test both.
4. [Combobox] Options prop shrinking while an option is active, then Enter, throws TypeError (6 options, ArrowDown x5, rerender with 2 options, Enter). Derive the effective active index each render, e.g. `const current = active !== null && enabled.includes(active) ? active : null;`, and use it for aria-activedescendant, data-active, Enter and arrow stepping.
5. [Combobox] A `value` matching no option (e.g. "zzz") makes blur call onChange(null) without user edits. Only clear (onChange(null)) on blur/Enter when the user actually typed the text down to empty (e.g. track that the text was edited: `filtering && text.trim() === ""`); whitespace-only counts as empty.
6. [Combobox] Always render the `<ul role="listbox">` (with `hidden` when closed) so `aria-controls` always references an existing element; options and the "No results" message only render while open. Make sure existing tests that check the listbox is absent when closed are updated to check it's not visible / hidden instead (queryByRole('listbox') returns null for hidden elements, which is fine).
7. [Dialog, Combobox] Consumer handlers in `...rest` are silently overridden. Chain them: Dialog `onKeyDown` (call consumer's first; skip internal handling if it called preventDefault); Combobox input `onKeyDown`, `onBlur`, `onClick` (call consumer's first). Combobox `id` from rest: use it as the input id if provided, else the generated one.
8. README.md: package.json has `"private": true`, so replace the `pnpm add @acme/ui react react-dom` install line with a sentence that it's consumed from this repo/workspace with react and react-dom 19 as peer deps. Update the Combobox/Dialog behaviour notes to match fixes 3 and 5 (Escape in an open combobox inside a dialog only closes the list; clearing to null happens only when the user empties the text).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Tabs
- T1. `<Tabs defaultValue? value? onValueChange?>` wraps `<TabList aria-label>`, `<Tab value disabled?>`, `<TabPanel value>`. Exported types: `TabsProps`, `TabListProps`, `TabProps`, `TabPanelProps`.
- T2. Roles/attrs: TabList is `role="tablist"` with its aria-label (and `aria-orientation="horizontal"` optional); each Tab is a `<button type="button" role="tab">` with a unique `id`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls` = its panel id; each TabPanel is `role="tabpanel"` with `aria-labelledby` = its tab id and `tabIndex={0}`; non-selected panels are `hidden` (or not rendered) so only the selected panel is visible.
- T3. Only the selected tab has `tabIndex=0`; all others `-1`. If nothing is selected (no defaultValue/value, or the selected value is disabled / matches no tab), the first enabled tab is the one with tabIndex 0 (and is shown as selected in uncontrolled mode) so the tablist is always reachable with Tab.
- T4. ArrowRight/ArrowLeft move focus to next/previous enabled tab, wrapping around at both ends, skipping disabled tabs; Home/End move to the first/last *enabled* tab. Selection follows focus: moving focus selects that tab (calls `onValueChange(value)`; in uncontrolled mode updates the panel). Other keys do nothing and keys must call `preventDefault` only for handled keys.
- T5. Clicking an enabled tab selects it; a disabled tab has `aria-disabled="true"` (or `disabled`), cannot be selected by click, and is never reached by arrows/Home/End.
- T6. Controlled: when `value` is passed, the component renders that value and only calls `onValueChange`; if the parent ignores the change, selection does not move (but focus may). Uncontrolled: `defaultValue` sets the initial tab; state is internal; `onValueChange` still fires.
- T7. Tab registration order follows DOM order even when tabs are rendered conditionally / reordered (e.g. query `[role=tab]` within the tablist element at key time rather than relying on registration order).
- Hostile: all tabs disabled (arrows do nothing, no crash); only one enabled tab (arrows keep focus on it, no repeated onValueChange spam for the same value is acceptable but no crash); `value` pointing at a nonexistent tab; two `<Tabs>` on one page must have distinct ids and independent keyboard handling.

Dialog
- D1. `<Dialog open onOpenChange title description? className? children>`; exported type `DialogProps`. When `open` is false nothing is rendered. When open, renders into `document.body` via a portal: a backdrop element and inside it (or beside it) an element with `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby` pointing at a heading rendering `title`, and `aria-describedby` pointing at an element rendering `description` only when description is given (no aria-describedby attribute otherwise).
- D2. On open, focus moves inside the dialog: to the first focusable element in the content, or to the dialog element itself (`tabIndex={-1}`) if there is none.
- D3. Focus trap: Tab from the last focusable element wraps to the first; Shift+Tab from the first (or from the dialog container itself) wraps to the last; with no focusable children focus stays on the dialog. Focusable query must skip disabled elements and `tabindex="-1"` and elements with `hidden`.
- D4. Escape calls `onOpenChange(false)` (pressed anywhere inside the dialog). A mouse click on the backdrop itself (not a click that started or ended inside the dialog panel — at minimum, clicks on dialog content must NOT close it) calls `onOpenChange(false)`.
- D5. When the dialog closes (open goes false, or the component unmounts while open), focus returns to the element that was focused right before it opened, if that element is still in the document.
- D6. Fully controlled by `open`: the dialog never closes itself; if the parent ignores `onOpenChange(false)`, it stays open.
- Hostile: dialog opened with no focusable children (focus on dialog, Tab keeps it there); trigger element removed from DOM while dialog open (closing must not throw); Escape inside a nested input still closes; two sequential open/close cycles each restore focus; SSR-safety not required but must not access `document` during render in a way that throws in jsdom.

Combobox
- C1. `<Combobox label options value onChange placeholder? className?>`, options `{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }`, `value: string | null`, `onChange(value: string | null)`. Exported types `ComboboxProps`, `ComboboxOption`. (Controlled via value/onChange as specified.)
- C2. Markup: a visible `<label>` associated with an `<input role="combobox">` (accessible name = label), `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded` true/false, `aria-controls` = listbox id, `placeholder` passed through. Popup is `<ul role="listbox">` (labelled by the label) with `<li role="option">` items each with unique id, `aria-selected` (true for the currently selected value), `aria-disabled="true"` for disabled.
- C3. When `value` is non-null the input shows the selected option's label; when value changes from parent, the input text updates to match. With the input text unchanged, the listbox shows all options.
- C4. Typing opens the listbox and filters options whose label contains the typed text case-insensitively (substring match; trimmed? -> match on raw text but treat whitespace-only like empty is acceptable). Regex/special characters like `(`, `.`, `*` are matched literally.
- C5. When no option matches, the popup shows a "No results" message (visible text exactly "No results"), not as a selectable option, and `aria-activedescendant` is absent; Enter does nothing.
- C6. ArrowDown opens the listbox if closed; when open, ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active option (input keeps DOM focus; input `aria-activedescendant` = active option id), skipping disabled options, and wrapping at the ends (wrap is acceptable; document whichever you choose). The active option is visually distinguishable via an attribute such as `data-active`. When filtering changes the list, the active option resets (to first enabled match or none). `aria-activedescendant` is removed when the list is closed or nothing is active.
- C7. Enter with an active option calls `onChange(option.value)`, sets input text to its label, closes the listbox. Clicking an enabled option does the same (use onMouseDown preventDefault or equivalent so input blur doesn't close before click). Clicking a disabled option does nothing.
- C8. Escape closes the listbox without calling onChange and restores the input text to the selected option's label (or '' if null). If already closed, Escape may clear nothing (do not call onChange).
- C9. Blur (focus leaving) closes the list and restores input text to the selected label without calling onChange. Clearing the input text to empty and then blurring/pressing Enter with no active option calls `onChange(null)` if value was non-null (document this).
- C10. Options where every option is disabled: arrows don't set an active option; no crash. Empty `options` array: typing shows "No results".
- Hostile: duplicate labels with different values (select picks the right value by id/index); option labels containing regex metacharacters; two comboboxes on one page with distinct ids; parent that ignores onChange (value stays, input text reverts on blur/escape).

General
- G1. `src/index.ts` exports Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel, Dialog, Combobox and all prop types listed above.
- G2. Tests per component in `src/*.test.tsx` using `@testing-library/react` + `@testing-library/user-event`, querying by role/accessible name, covering every criterion above including the hostile cases.
- G3. README.md documents install/usage, each component's props (table: name, type, required, description) and keyboard behavior (table), plus a short usage example per component and the commands `pnpm test` / `pnpm typecheck`.
- G4. `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` pass.

CHECKS: while working `pnpm vitest run src/Dialog.test.tsx` and `pnpm vitest run src/Combobox.test.tsx`; at the end `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck`, both must pass.
